coaching.headline: Serath kept dying, every Fangtooth came our way, and it was over fast. Clean fucking work.
coaching.team: A quick, clean stomp in which Serath died seven times. We drew first blood, took all three Fangtooths, the Mini Prime and the only Seedling, and took two of their outer towers for one of ours. The sloppy patch came when Murdock and Khaimera both died shortly before our only lost tower, and Sparrow later won one exchange. Those were the only blemishes. The closing ace, followed by the last Fangtooth, finished it.

focus.title: Dead jungler, free pit
focus.evidence: Each of our three Fangtooths and the Mini Prime fell to us within a minute of a Serath death. The record does not show whether the pit was already up when Serath died or who started it.
focus.action: Next game, whenever the enemy jungler dies and a Fangtooth or Prime is up, Xeebs calls it and the two nearest players start it before the respawn. Check that every such death ends in a take.

perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Gadget was the cleanest game in the lobby: seven kills without a death, the richest player on the map, farm well above Willy's usual pace. Serath died to Gadget three times, a hell of a way to tell a jungler to stay home. The gold outran the damage, with hero damage under Willy's usual Gadget rate. When Riktor lands a pull or a suppress next game, Gadget drops Tesla Dome on that target.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs ran the map. First blood on Revenant, three kills on Serath, roughly two thirds of our objective damage and the most healing in the lobby: that is a jungler setting the tempo, not following it. The one lost exchange came when Sparrow killed Khaimera and Legion. Next game, when the enemy carry is alive in a fight, Khaimera saves Ambush for that carry once she is hurt, because the leap hits harder on a wounded target.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock topped our hero damage and kept punishing two enemy laners: Gideon died to Mr_Meat31 three times and Revenant twice. Fucking good. The recurring problem was Revenant himself, whose only two kills of the game were both on Murdock. If Revenant shows up next game with Reckoning available, Murdock keeps Buckshot for him: the push-back buys distance and the armor shred adds damage to the trade, so Revenant has to earn the next one.
perPlayer.3aa472b8-db6f-494b-967e-54c3408fc466: NO_LIFE_KING_HS kept Legion alive, one death against a usual count of nearly five, and opened the closing ace with kills on Zinx and Sparrow. Keep that restraint. The soft spot was output: hero damage ran more than a third under that player's own Legion norm. Press the Advantage drops a Rally Point at every takedown and speeds up Legion's fire, so when one lands mid-fight, Legion keeps shooting from inside it instead of backing off.
perPlayer.07237cc8-a80d-4b8b-ae3e-9347f8c34a9e: Riktor was a fucking wall: no deaths and the most damage mitigated in the lobby. The rest of the support job was thin. Riktor had a hand in under a third of our kills and placed three wards to Zinx's eight, clearing none. Rift Walkers raises the ward cap for exactly this. Before the next Fangtooth, Riktor spends every ward charge on the enemy approach and walks in with Riplash ready, so the pull starts the fight.

matchup: Legion and Riktor faced Sparrow and Zinx, and neither duo lost a player early.
Sparrow killed Khaimera and Legion in the one lost exchange; Legion took Sparrow and Zinx in the closing ace.
Zinx was the enemy healer, and Sparrow's Vanquisher executes a hero who drops very low.
build: Manta Scythe and Resolution both add physical penetration, which feeds the K-75 Storm Rifle.
The common winning core is Malady, Deathstalker and Spear Of Desolation; no fight here shows the build costing anything.
eternal: Marrow, Blood Bank and Jealousy are a sustain-and-trade package, and one death says the survival side held.
The Maw is the slot-two alternative, true damage into low-health targets, when finishing matters more than trading from low health.
augment: Press the Advantage's Rally Point raises Legion's rate of fire and gives nearby allies attack speed after a takedown.
It pays in extended fights that produce takedowns, like the closing ace, and gives nothing in an exchange without a kill.
crest: Eviscerator's burst of attack speed, omnivamp and on-hit damage suits Legion's sustained fire and stacks with Marrow's healing.
improvement: Survival held, so hero damage is the build question.
Tainted Rounds is the comparison against Manta Scythe, trading penetration, lifesteal and faster farming for anti-heal against Zinx and Serath.
No enemy finished an armor item, so Deathstalker's shred is less urgent; this win does not prove the swap was needed.

matchup: Zinx was their healer, and Riktor's pull, silence and suppress are the tools to start fights on her or Sparrow.
Gideon's Astral Catalyst hits shielded targets harder, and Riktor's Electrocute shield and Transference both lean on shields.
build: Transference adds health, both armors, and movement speed and armor while shielded, with Electrocute's shield as the trigger.
It was the only finished item; Riktor led the lobby in damage mitigated, but Transference's share is not shown.
eternal: Knell's Rust shreds both armors on hero hits and gives Riktor part of it; Patina's shield turns on Transference's bonus.
That favors a frontline support who trades hits, and Riktor's zero deaths say the durability side held.
augment: Zap O' 9-Chains turns ability casts into a zap on nearby enemies, extra damage in grouped fights.
It adds no crowd control, so the pull, silence and suppress remain the main job.
crest: Rift Walkers' dash pulls nearby heroes, a second engage tool beside Riplash and Skewer.
Rift Walkers was built for vision work, but three wards against Zinx's eight does not reflect that.
improvement: The winning core is Dynamo, Xenia and Frosted Lure, and Dynamo fits Riplash and Skewer directly.
Compared with Transference, that trades Riktor's own shield value for damage and protection the team shares.
Riktor never died but had a hand in under a third of our kills, so the next item should serve participation.

matchup: Revenant got both of his kills on Murdock; Murdock killed Revenant twice and Gideon three times.
Revenant's Reckoning pulls a single target into a separate realm with him and slows them, forcing a one-on-one.
build: Lightning Hawk and Vanquisher both add critical chance; neither adds sustain or defense.
They are the first two items of the common winning core, and no fight here shows the build costing anything.
eternal: Melting Point needs targets above a high physical armor threshold, and no enemy finished an armor item.
Sub-Surface, less damage from area abilities, is the slot-two alternative against Gideon's area spells.
augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired pierce units and reach farther, rewarding poking from a safe distance and firing through the wave.
crest: Pacifier is both the finisher and the exit: a dash, an empowered physical hit and a recast after a kill.
Against Revenant's Reckoning, the dash is the tool to hold back.
improvement: Imperator, the natural next item, completes the winning core with more critical strike damage.
If Revenant keeps finding Murdock first, a defensive slot trades that crit damage for survival.
This match does not prove either choice was needed.

matchup: Gadget killed Gideon, their main magical damage dealer, twice and Serath three times without dying.
Serath's dive is the kit-level threat to an immobile mage, and Security Gate's root is the answer.
build: Soulbinder deals bonus damage on ability hits from long range; Azure Core and Oblivion Crown add power.
The winning core runs Entropy and Overseer instead of Soulbinder and Oblivion Crown; no fight shows the build costing anything.
eternal: Runic Focus scales power with current mana, which suits Azure Core and Soulbinder's mana pools.
Bottomless Vial pays only for River Buffs Gadget personally kills, and the record does not show whose they were.
Perfection, ability haste above a high health threshold, is the slot-two alternative for a mage who did not die.
augment: Auto-Lock Amp makes the Seek and Destroy droid's damage zone harder to walk out of.
Its value depends on stopping the droid over a hero, which the record cannot show.
crest: Tempest damages up to three nearby heroes and heals, a close-range tool that pays inside the fight, such as Tesla Dome.
improvement: The gold outran the damage; Overseer, from the winning core, makes Tesla Dome hit harder and heals Gadget.
Entropy adds extra damage to each ability hit; both give up Soulbinder's long-range bonus for steadier damage in close fights.
This win does not prove the swap; it is the next comparison.

matchup: Serath died seven times, three of them to Khaimera, and got both of her kills on Khaimera.
The enemy ran three physical damage dealers, Sparrow, Revenant and Serath, plus Zinx's healing.
build: Ashbringer cuts non-ultimate cooldowns on each basic attack, and Claw Of Hermes drains mana and gives Unleash extra attacks.
Neither item adds armor, and Khaimera took the most damage in the lobby.
eternal: Exarch is a support Eternal here: healing or shielding, like Invigorate's heal, grants attack speed and magical on-hit damage.
Marrow is the bruiser alternative, trading the team healing for lifesteal that grows at low health.
augment: Jungle Invasion rewards invading, doubled in the enemy jungle; Serath's deaths fit, though where they happened is not shown.
crest: Judgement's area damage, healing on hero hits and omnivamp fit a sustain duelist and add to lobby-leading healing.
improvement: The armor gap is the build question: no armor against three physical threats while absorbing the most damage.
Sky Splitter and Onixian Quiver complete the winning core, adding lifesteal and mitigation that grows with missing health.
If Serath or Sparrow keep finding kills, compare an armor item against Claw Of Hermes, trading Unleash's extra attacks and mana burn.

threats: Heal-stacking: Zinx. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s), Gadget Security Gate (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
ourKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
ourKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
ourKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Security Gate root → Sticky Mine → Tesla Dome zone ult
ourKits.winCondition: root with the gate and trap a fight inside the Tesla Dome
ourKits.passive: FDA stacks grant scaling magical power
ourKits.playWith: frontline that holds enemies in her Dome
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge the gate; spread vs the Dome — she's immobile, dive her

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Scar mark → Obliterate homing missiles → Reckoning 1v1 realm ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Reckoning a target into the Nether Realm and crit them down 1v1
enemyKits.playWith: a team to clean up if his 1v1 stalls
enemyKits.playAgainst: the ult is a 1v1 — peel the realmed ally can't help, so don't be caught alone; he's crit-reliant early-weak

enemyKits.combo: Ricochet stun → Bad Medicine zone → Infuse heal an ally → Neural Regenesis revive
enemyKits.winCondition: keep an ally alive with Infuse + the revive ult and poke with Ricochet
enemyKits.playWith: a carry she can pocket-heal and revive
enemyKits.playAgainst: she can't heal herself — dive HER; bait the revive before committing

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up
